Infinx Healthcare (founded 2012, headquartered in Cupertino, CA / Spring, TX) is primarily an AI-powered revenue cycle management (RCM) and patient access solutions company — not an EHR vendor. The certified EHR product traces back to **iMed Software Corp** (founded 2002 in Louisiana), which built **iMedEMR**, a cloud-based ambulatory EHR and practice management system.\n     9→\n    10→**Acquisition chain:**\n    11→1. **iMed Software Corp** built iMedEMR (certified by Drummond Group).\n    12→2. **i3 Verticals (NASDAQ: IIIV)** acquired iMed Software on April 30, 2022. The product was rebranded as **i3Med** and became part of i3 Verticals Healthcare's broader platform alongside their existing billing products (HPlusPro/Healthpac).\n    13→3. **Infinx Healthcare** acquired i3 Verticals' entire Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management business in May 2025 for $96 million. This acquisition brought the EHR product (and its ONC certification) under Infinx's umbrella.\n    14→\n    15→The CHPL product number for v5.3 (`15.04.04.2621.iMed.53.02.1.241219`) still contains \"iMed\" in the identifier, confirming the product's origin. The EHR product appears to be a secondary/inherited asset from the i3 Verticals acquisition rather than Infinx's core offering. It is a fully integrated EHR + PM solution designed for ambulatory medical organizations, providing clinical documentation, practice management, scheduling, billing, and patient engagement in a single platform. The CHPL metadata indicates intended users are \"Nurses, Doctors, Administrative\" staff.\n    26→\n    27→The product is certified for a substantial set of ONC criteria including:\n    28→- **Clinical data**: (a)(2) CPOE for medications, (a)(3) CPOE for diagnostic imaging, (a)(5) demographics, (a)(12) family health history, (a)(14) implantable device list\n    29→- **Transitions of care**: (b)(1) and (b)(2) for clinical information exchange via C-CDA\n    30→- **Patient portal**: (e)(1) view, download, transmit\n    31→- **Public health reporting**: (f)(3) electronic case reporting, and (f)(5) electronic reporting for cancer registries (v5.4 only)\n    32→- **FHIR/API access**: (g)(7)-(g)(10) for standardized API access\n    33→- **Clinical quality**: (c)(1) clinical quality measures\n    34→\n    35→### Users & Market\n    36→\n    37→**Target users**: Primary care physicians, specialists in multi-disciplinary ambulatory practices, nurses, and administrative/billing staff. Once downloaded, the file can be unzipped to reveal\na folder of files. The folder will contain the following files:\n.csv files - these include all the patient data in patient tables. The files will have a header row with the field names listed, followed by the\npatient data in a comma-separated format. Find definitions of each field name in the below Patient Data Tables.\n.xml files - there will be one main ccda.xml that will be an export of all patient ccda-compatible data. There may be other ccda files with a\n32-digit id after ccda_ in the file name (ie. ccda_123456789.xml). These ccda’s are referrals and their associated referral information can be\nfound in the patient_referrals csv by cross-referencing the ccda_id inside this csv with the filename.\n.pdf files - There are several types of files that may be exported as PDFs.\nSoapDoc_ files include all visit data from a particular patient visit.\ndocument_ files are chart documents that may have been scanned or otherwise uploaded into the patient chart.\nLabs_ files are PDF lab results.\nformletter_ files are letters the clinic has generated inside the patient’s chart\nOB_ files include all pregnancy-related visit data\n\nPatient Data Tables\npatientinfo - contains basic identifying information about the patient (dob, chart number, ssn), demographic information for the patient, and\nsome medical or social history questions as customized by the clinic.\ncharges - all CPT charges associated with the patient’s account\nhealthmaintenance - scheduled recurrent diagnostic labs or tests the provider associated with the patient\nob - OB report of pregnancy-related visits\npatient_advforms - online patient forms\npatient_codes - codes of various code systems associated with the patient\npatient_forms_data - forms filled out for the patient\npatient_guarantor - guarantor information and demographics associated with the patient\npatient_letters - letters written by the clinic that are associated with the patient\npatient_pmp - prescription monitoring program database results for the patient\npatient_referrals - referrals sent out to other providers on behalf of the patient\nptinr - if the patient requires periodic prothrombin time(PT) and international normalized ratio(INR) tests, this documents the reason for the\ntest and the frequency decided by the The data dictionary covers 248 fields across 15 tables — not a trivial export. The generic `patient_codes` table may contain some of this data, but it's underdocumented.\n\nThe documentation quality is **adequate but not exemplary**. Each has a header row with field names followed by comma-separated data.\n\n2. **XML files** — a main `ccda.xml` containing all C-CDA-compatible clinical data, plus additional `ccda_[id].xml` files for referrals (cross-referenced via the `patient_referrals` CSV's `ccda_id` field).\n\n3. **PDF files** with specific prefixes:\n   - `SoapDoc_` — visit/encounter SOAP notes\n   - `document_` — scanned/uploaded chart documents\n   - `Labs_` — lab results\n   - `formletter_` — clinic-generated letters\n   - `OB_` — pregnancy-related visit data\n\n### Data Dictionary\n\nThe documentation defines **15 patient data tables** with **248 total fields**:\n\n| Table | Description | Fields |\n|-------|-------------|--------|\n| patientinfo | Demographics, identifiers, social/medical history | 46 |\n| charges | CPT charges, billing data | 21 |\n| healthmaintenance | Scheduled recurrent diagnostic tests | 10 |\n| ob | Pregnancy-related visits | 8 |\n| patient_advforms | Online patient forms with responses | 11 |\n| patient_codes | Codes from various code systems | 14 |\n| patient_forms_data | Provider-side forms with responses | 6 |\n| patient_guarantor | Guarantor demographics and billing info | 22 |\n| patient_letters | Clinic-generated letters | 8 |\n| patient_pmp | Prescription monitoring program results | 10 |\n| patient_referrals | Provider referrals with C-CDA cross-references | 12 |\n| ptinr | PT/INR anticoagulation tracking plans | 8 |\n| ptinr_log | PT/INR test result logs | 15 |\n| schedules | Appointment data with billing fields | 42 |\n| surgerymemo | Surgical documentation (custom/optional) | 8 |\n\nMost tables include a Schema column documenting data types (32-digit GUIDs, dates as Y-m-d, timestamps, integers, text, JSON arrays). **Scanned documents** — Exported as `document_` PDFs\n- **C-CDA clinical summary** — The main `ccda.xml` covers standard clinical data (problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, etc.)\n\n**Domains that appear missing or underdocumented:**\n- **Medication lists / prescriptions** — No dedicated CSV table for active medications, prescription history, or e-prescribing records. Medications may be captured in the C-CDA XML or within `patient_codes`, but there's no explicit medication table. Given the product's DrFirst e-prescribing integration, this is a notable gap.\n- **Allergy lists** — Similarly no dedicated allergy table. Likely in C-CDA only.\n- **Problem lists / diagnoses** — No dedicated diagnosis table. The generic `patient_codes` table may hold ICD codes, but this isn't explicitly documented. Likely in C-CDA or SOAP note PDFs.\n- **Immunizations** — No dedicated table; likely in C-CDA.\n- **Insurance/enrollment information** — No insurance coverage table documenting payer details, policy numbers, coverage dates. `financial_class` in patientinfo is a single field. The `type` field presumably differentiates them, but no value set is documented.\n- SOAP note PDFs (`SoapDoc_`) likely contain rich clinical data (vitals, assessments, plans) but in unstructured PDF form, not as queryable structured data.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a **hybrid approach**:\n- **CSV files** for structured patient data tables — a vendor-proprietary schema, not a recognized standard\n- **C-CDA XML** for clinical data that maps to the C-CDA standard\n- **PDF files** for clinical notes, lab results, scanned documents, and other unstructured content\n\nThis is a reasonable and honest approach to b(10) — it doesn't pretend FHIR or C-CDA covers everything. The CSV tables export data that genuinely doesn't fit neatly into C-CDA (billing charges, guarantor info, PMP scores, custom forms). The C-CDA captures standardized clinical data.\n\n**Strengths:**\n- The export clearly goes beyond USCDI/US Core — billing data, guarantor demographics, PMP scores, custom forms with JSON responses, surgical memos, anticoagulation tracking\n- Relationships between tables use consistent 32-digit GUIDs (patientid, scheduleid)\n- C-CDA referral documents are cross-referenced to the `patient_referrals` CSV via `ccda_id`\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- No formal schema file (no XSD, JSON Schema, or DDL). The PDF data dictionary is the only specification.\n- CSV relationships are implicit via shared GUIDs — no foreign key documentation\n- No sample export files provided\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Readability:** The PDF is well-organized with a clear structure: overview → file types → table index → table-by-table field definitions. Each table has a summary description followed by field-level details.\n\n**Field-level detail:** 11 of 15 tables include data types (Schema column). The `schedules` table notably lists ~35 fields without any descriptions — just bare field names. The `patientinfo` table has descriptions but no data types.\n\n**Value sets:** A few coded fields document their values (e.g., `chrGender`: 1=male, 2=female; `status`: 0=active, 1=inactive; `caseType`: New/Pending/Processed). Most coded fields lack value set documentation.\n\n**Missing:**\n- No worked examples or sample export files\n- No user guide for performing the export (referenced but not provided publicly)\n- No versioning or change history\n- No documentation of relationships between tables beyond the ccda_id cross-reference\n- The `patient_codes` table's `type` field is the key to understanding what clinical data is exported as structured codes, but its possible values are not documented\n\nA developer could import this data based on the documentation, but would need significant trial-and-error to understand the `patient_codes` and `patient_forms_data` tables fully.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation provides table-level and field-level granularity, which is better than many vendors. The data dictionary covers 248 fields across 15 tables — not a trivial export. However:\n\n- **Granularity is uneven**: `charges` has full field/description/schema documentation; `schedules` has 35 undocumented fields; `patientinfo` has no data types.\n- **No relationship documentation**: Tables share GUIDs (patientid, scheduleid) but no ER diagram or foreign key mapping.\n- **No value set catalog**: Coded fields like `patient_codes.type`, `patient_codes.code`, `patient_advforms.status` have minimal value documentation.\n- **No versioning**: The filename suggests creation date of 2023-12-19. No indication of updates since then despite the product version advancing from 5.1 to 5.4.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nThis is a **genuine b(10) effort** — the vendor has created a real EHI export that goes beyond just C-CDA/USCDI. The export includes billing data, custom forms, guarantor information, prescription monitoring scores, and other data that wouldn't appear in a FHIR or C-CDA-only export. The hybrid CSV + C-CDA + PDF approach is practical and honest.\n\nHowever, the export has **meaningful gaps in clinical structured data**. The generic `patient_codes` table may contain some of this data, but it's underdocumented.\n\nThe documentation quality is **adequate but not exemplary**.
